cells.tense: You are keeping the exchange level between the people you are tending.
cells.ask: Keep the shape of one thing you tend exactly as it stands — no additions, no trimming — and find out whether steady is enough on its own.
cells.core:
What you tend — a person, a patch of work, something young — is getting what it needs, and the exchange has settled even. Nothing has to be added to hurry it, nothing pulled back to test it. On a good day this is tending something through a season without once asking what it hands back.

Keep the shape of one thing you tend exactly as it stands — no additions, no trimming — and find out whether steady is enough on its own. You'll feel a pull to improve it or to step away; neither is called for. What you've built is feeding what comes next, and the feed is quiet, and that's enough.
cells.sheetLine: Steady hands, even exchange — nothing has to be proved this week.
cells.verb: giving and receiving kept level between people
cells.place: where what is growing is tended

cells.tense: You are pouring into what is growing faster than it can take.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Where you've been carrying more than your half for something you're raising, set the surplus down and let whoever it belongs to lift it.
cells.core:
You've gotten out past the thing you tend. The finish is already clear to you, and you're watering a plant still deciding how to stand — extra feeds, more attention, checking whether what you gave came home. From inside, it feels like care. From the other side it reads as pressure, and some of what you're growing is learning to lean rather than root.

Set the surplus down. Whatever you've been carrying past your half for something you're raising — the hour, the worry, the arranging — leave that portion with whoever it belongs to. It'll be lighter for both of you, and you'll learn what the thing does when it isn't propped. Strength here contains without squeezing.

cells.tense: You stopped showing up where something was growing, and that door is behind you now.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Take a thing you once tended and set down what it actually needs now, a line each. Cross off anything not true this month, then do the smallest one.
cells.core:
Something you were tending has gone quiet. The plant's still there, the person still is, but your hands haven't been in it — and if asked, you'd say you stepped back to let it grow. Part of you sits at a door that closed, waiting for a signal to go back in. The waiting takes the hours the work would use.

Take a thing you once tended and set down what it actually needs now, a line each. Cross off anything not true this month. The list gets short. What's left is one or two real things, and one of them is small enough to do soon. That coming-close, carefully, is how you walk back in.
cells.sheetLine: You left, and you're still at the door.

cells.tense: What is growing stays level under your hand while you say you've stepped back.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: As you check on what you're growing, carry both facts at once — it's fine, and you're minding it — and hold them where no one can hear.
cells.core:
One growing thing keeps coming out even, and the hand keeping it even is yours — though if you were asked, you'd say it holds steady without you. It does fine by itself. It also eats from your hand each day, water you don't count, small shifts so nothing tips. The minding is real and it's yours, and the story you tell has you farther off than you stand.

As you check on what you're growing, carry both facts at once — it's fine, and you're minding it — and hold them where no one can hear. Nothing else changes. You'll feel the hold, and after a week the quiet minding will feel like something you chose rather than something you don't mention.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping it alive, and saying you don't.

attempts.check: The draft's riskiest claim is reading Too Much as somebody who tends past the point the thing needed and now braces for a result that hasn't arrived; the record supports only excess in the seat, and the person could reasonably say they tend less than they used to. The asks survive a wrong read because each one is small, material, and done alone — none requires the read to be true to be worth an afternoon. The sentence serving me more than them is any line where the tenderness sounds like a verdict on how they love; those are cut and the cells now say what the hands do, not what the heart lacks.
